## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

The chain above is the third run of this chain. The two earlier runs were on the previous candidate `02ee1f049a40`, which was rewritten into this candidate before any push: its code, spec, tests, fixtures, topology and contract are byte-identical to this candidate, which adds only `docs/runbooks/freeipa-dns-client.md`. They gave identical results to this record (L1 pass, L3 `failed=0` on all three nodes, L4 `failed=0`, L5 24/0/0, L6 `changed=0`, the same per-host PLAY RECAP counts). The first record listed more vault key names than the chain needs, so the second and this run use a `-e @file` holding only `ipa_admin_password`. The arms below ran once, against `02ee1f049a40`, and were not repeated because the execution-affecting files are byte-identical.

**Method.** The arms below ran on a persistent copy of this topology (FreeIPA server that is also its own consumer, Ubuntu 24.04 dns tier that is also a consumer, AlmaLinux 9 consumer): `topology up`, the chain applied with the BASE tree (L1, L3, L4, L5 21/0/0 for C1-C7, L6 `changed=0`), a snapshot `healthy`. Before every arm all three nodes were rolled back to `healthy` and the fault was injected over SSH. Then BASE (clean `git archive` of main at `6d320073`, the 7-row spec) and CANDIDATE (clean `git archive` of `02ee1f049a40`, the previous candidate, the 8-row spec) each ran, from that same snapshot: `pilot verify docs/verification/freeipa-dns-client.md` (before), `ansible-playbook ... freeipa-dns-client-apply.yml -l <host> -e stage=sandbox --check --diff`, the real apply, verify again, and a second apply. The chain above is the fresh-target proof; the arms are fault injection on a once-applied host. Every fault was injected, none was observed naturally.

**D4, the gate firing on a real host** (CANDIDATE apply): the first read after the write found `<FreeIPA>, <dnsmasq>`, `nmcli general reload dns-rc` ran (rc 0), the re-read for 10 seconds found the same list, and the gate failed with: "after writing <dns tier>, <FreeIPA> the resolver glibc uses is <FreeIPA>, <dnsmasq>. Read from /etc/resolv.conf. Not in the list this run wrote: <dnsmasq>. nmcli general reload dns-rc was run (rc=0) and the file still did not match after 10 seconds: something other than the connection profile pilot manages decides what NetworkManager writes (for example a global-dns setting ...)". The rescue then reported "Rollback: /etc/resolv.conf restored; connection 'System eth0' DNS settings restored; device eth0 reapplied" and the host's `resolv.conf` and profile were the same as before the run.

**Never-applied hosts** (rolled back to the pre-apply snapshot): `--check --diff` of the CANDIDATE playbook on the AlmaLinux host without `dig` (rc 0, report printed, "pilot does not manage this host's resolver yet") and on the Ubuntu host (rc 0, report names the stub and the servers behind it from `resolvectl dns`). The C8 probe through `pilot verify --probe` printed `resolver-effective-wrong dig-not-found` on the AlmaLinux host and `resolver-effective-wrong stub=127.0.0.53 ... 192.168.122.1=no_address(NXDOMAIN)` on the Ubuntu host. The L3 dry-run of the chain above did the same on the three fresh ephemeral nodes.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

- The gate failing on Debian/Ubuntu is covered only by the localhost harness (a fake resolv.conf and fake `nmcli`/`resolvectl`): the role writes that file itself, so no real fault could be produced there. The `nmcli general reload dns-rc` repair and the 10-second re-read ran on NetworkManager 1.54.3 / AlmaLinux 9 only; no other EL release and no Ubuntu host with NetworkManager.
- `dig` 9.16 (AlmaLinux 9) and 9.18 (Ubuntu 24.04) only; C8 under `sh`/`bash`/`dash` in the local harness, `dash` and `bash` on the VMs. IPv6 nameservers, `%scope` ids, `options rotate`, and a `nameserver` line whose address does not parse (glibc skips it, C8 counts it as one of the first 3 and reports `no_answer`) are not covered. The `+norec` ban is a textual check.
- C8 asks only for the FreeIPA server FQDN. Whether other internal zones are routed to FreeIPA DNS (the issue's `~domain` routing domain) is out of scope by decision, as are `pilot doctor`, new inventory variables and `internal/diagnose`.
- The gate is fail-closed for every host that runs the shared resolver file: `freeipa-dns-client` and the `internal-endpoint` fleet baseline. A host with a deliberate extra resolver source (NetworkManager global-dns naming a server this run does not write, the systemd-resolved stub) now fails there until the source is removed. `internal-endpoint` ran only as `--tags C9 -l <host>` (its reconcile play matched no host); no `pilot deploy` or `pilot reconcile` run.
- The arms are fault injection on once-applied hosts rolled back from a snapshot; fresh-host behavior is the ephemeral chain and the never-applied-host arm. BASE arms ran before the candidate was frozen but against the unchanged base tree. The dns tier answered exactly as the older captures in `testdata/dig-nscheck`; those are reused rather than re-captured.
- The dns tier ran with built-in defaults and without `services: local` (the host cache stack was not up on this machine).
